Resubmitted. This round I addressed the two open points and re-validated (ok:true).

**Changes made:**

1. **IP limb re-drafted to remove circularity and to name the deliverable-type subject matter** — limb (d) now reads: *"an allegation that the RevMed Licensed Technology, any materials or deliverables provided by RevMed, or Sanofi's exercise of the licenses granted to it under this Agreement, infringes or misappropriates the intellectual property rights of a Third Party"*. Dropping "any Third Party Claim alleging that" cures the redundancy against the Section 14.1 lead-in, and adding "materials or deliverables provided by RevMed" gives the indemnity an express deliverables hook — the closest available analogue to "Services or Deliverables" in an agreement that has neither defined term. This is a broadening in our favour, not a concession.
2. **Cross-reference check completed before sending** — the only references to Section 14.2 anywhere in the Agreement are generic (Section 14.3(a)/(b) procedure, Section 14.5 liability carve-out, the defined-term index entry for "RevMed Indemnitee"), and Section 12.x/Article XIV survival at p0522 refers to Sanofi's Article XIV indemnity as a whole. Nothing cross-refers to the narrowed 14.2(a)–(d) limbs, so no conforming change is needed elsewhere; the residual commercial pushback risk from removing Sanofi's Commercialization and negligence indemnities is flagged for the negotiator.

**Unchanged:** limbs (e) data breach and (f) RevMed's breach of Applicable Law; the "(a) through (f)" conforming lead-in; the narrowed Section 14.2 with "[Intentionally omitted.]" placeholders preserving lettering; and Section 14.3's notice/control/cooperation machinery and Section 14.5's preservation of uncapped indemnity claims, both left untouched. The remaining deterministic flag is the known vocabulary artefact ("Services"/"Deliverables" do not exist in this collaboration agreement); the substantive Vendor IP indemnity is now in operative text at Section 14.1(d).
